newsitem.title: CHINA: China's students want to join Communist Party.
newsitem.headline: China's students want to join Communist Party.

text.p: About one-third of China's college students want to join the ruling Communist Party, and most were confident about the current political situation, said a survey published in the People's Daily on Monday.
The government survey looked at the political awareness among students in 58 colleges and universities in six cities and provinces last year, the newspaper said.

More than 90 percent of students said they thought China's current political situation was stable, while more than 80 percent thought the government had achieved remarkable successes in reform and opening up to the outside world, it said.
About one-third were eager to join the 57-million-member Communist Party, regarded by many as a major route to success in China.
Another survey of college students in China's capital, Beijing, found that the number who wanted to to into business had slumped to 0.7 percent this year from 34.3 percent in 1993.
About 48.6 percent of the students planned to continue their education after graduating, said the survey by a Beijing government department in early 1997. It gave no further details.

The surveys showed little sign of the disenchantment with China's system that brought students onto the streets in May and June of 1989 to demand more democracy. Those demonstrations were crushed by the army with heavy loss of life on June 4, 1989.
